body: Annes suggested I ping you @weinig about this. I'm hoping we can collectively move on this relatively quickly and eliminate a class of bugs.

<details>
<summary>AI feedback</summary>

Reviewed at 8dd16a0. CI passes and the branch merges cleanly with main. The three changed steps look right: `SafePromiseResolve` takes a PromiseCapability Record, the `!` assertions still hold because the built-in resolving functions can't throw, a thenable's `then()` is still called in the same microtask as before, and leaving the reject paths alone makes sense.

**Blockers**

- [HostObjectHasImpureLookupInternalMethods](https://tc39.es/proposal-thenable-curtailment/#sec-hosthasinternalmethodswhichcanrunusercode) isn't defined for Web IDL's objects, so it defaults to false. Legacy platform objects that support named properties need it: [LegacyPlatformObjectGetOwnProperty](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/8dd16a0258e95f9cf560531687f82b49b63d47db/index.bs#L14283) runs the [named property visibility algorithm](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/8dd16a0258e95f9cf560531687f82b49b63d47db/index.bs#L14217-L14221), which calls `[[GetPrototypeOf]]` and "has an own property" up a mutable prototype chain. For example, with `<form name=then>` and `Object.setPrototypeOf(HTMLCollection.prototype, new Proxy(…))`, resolving with `document.forms` (e.g., by returning it from a `pull()`) makes [PropertyAccessCouldRunUserCode](https://tc39.es/proposal-thenable-curtailment/#sec-has-property-which-could-run-user-code)'s `! o.[[GetOwnProperty]]("then")` run the Proxy's traps synchronously, which breaks its "do not run user code" assertion. There's an interop angle too: Gecko implements these objects and `WindowProxy` as engine-level proxies, and the [README's experiment](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-thenable-curtailment/blob/c162ea93667a61f4a07868a35e4964942ce885a1/README.md#experiment-webidl) already saw an extra tick when resolving with a `WindowProxy`, which the spec as written doesn't predict. The hook could return true for those that lack `[LegacyOverrideBuiltIns]` (with it, the visibility algorithm returns before walking the chain), or for all legacy platform objects. It would also be good to say (in HTML) whether `WindowProxy` and `Location` count. Either way this needs tests.
- web-platform-tests/wpt#64001 doesn't update [streams/readable-byte-streams/patched-global.any.js](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/8a5805234c70967e448b07eb8ae86155f0bf4299/streams/readable-byte-streams/patched-global.any.js#L40), which asserts that an `Object.prototype.then` getter runs synchronously during `controller.enqueue()`. With this change the getter is deferred, so that test fails (the README lists it as a failure).

**Suggestions**

- Consider clarifying the scope in the PR description. It says async iteration is left alone, but the async sequence algorithms [get the next value](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/8dd16a0258e95f9cf560531687f82b49b63d47db/index.bs#L8385) and [close an async iterator](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/8dd16a0258e95f9cf560531687f82b49b63d47db/index.bs#L8417) use "a promise resolved with", so they change too. Only `next()` and `return()` on asynchronous iterator prototype objects ([1](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/8dd16a0258e95f9cf560531687f82b49b63d47db/index.bs#L13161), [2](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/8dd16a0258e95f9cf560531687f82b49b63d47db/index.bs#L13250)) keep calling `[[Resolve]]`. Also, the change to [converting to a promise type](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/8dd16a0258e95f9cf560531687f82b49b63d47db/index.bs#L8580) affects callback return values (e.g., Streams' `pull()`), not just arguments.
- Consider adding a note to those `next()` and `return()` steps saying they intentionally keep calling `[[Resolve]]` to match [AsyncGeneratorCompleteStep](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-asyncgeneratorcompletestep), so it doesn't read as an oversight.
- Consider adding a note to [resolve](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/8dd16a0258e95f9cf560531687f82b49b63d47db/index.bs#L8651) stating the new guarantee: resolving a promise never synchronously runs JavaScript. It could also mention the edge case that a value with a `then` getter returning a non-callable now fulfills one microtask later.
- Consider which realm is used. `SafePromiseResolve` creates `deferredThen` in the current realm, and the job takes its realm from that function, where it used to come from the `then` function. HTML's [HostEnqueuePromiseJob](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#hostenqueuepromisejob) uses that realm to decide whether the job runs at all. As [resolve](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/8dd16a0258e95f9cf560531687f82b49b63d47db/index.bs#L8657) takes no realm and is often invoked from tasks, this is underdefined (see #371 and #932). Creating `deferredThen` in the promise's realm (upstream), or having Web IDL specify the realm, would avoid that.
- As this appears to be your first contribution here, consider adding yourself to the [Acknowledgments](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/8dd16a0258e95f9cf560531687f82b49b63d47db/index.bs#L15325).

**Nits**

- [`url: sec-safe-resolve-promise`](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/8dd16a0258e95f9cf560531687f82b49b63d47db/index.bs#L96) points to the chapter heading; the operation is `sec-safe-promise-resolve` (as already suggested in review). The WPT comments link to the same chapter anchor.
- [fetch/api/response/response-body-read-task-handling.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/8a5805234c70967e448b07eb8ae86155f0bf4299/fetch/api/response/response-body-read-task-handling.html) now passes without testing what it was written for; consider updating it in web-platform-tests/wpt#64001 as well.
- Proposal FYI: the rendered draft still says "Stage 2 Draft", and [RequiresDeferredPromiseResolution](https://tc39.es/proposal-thenable-curtailment/#sec-requires-deferred-promise-resolution) calls `value.[[Get]]("then")` without a Receiver argument.

</details>

I checked the web compat impact of this change against the HTTP Archive crawl with an instrumented Chromium build. I couldn't find any page where it would make an observable difference: in a sample of 5,512 root pages, none resolved a Web IDL promise with a value whose `then` lookup could run script.

AI summary of the research ([noamr/webidl-safe-resolve-compat-1645](https://github.com/noamr/webidl-safe-resolve-compat-1645)):

> **Method.** A temporary probe in Blink's Web IDL promise resolution (`ScriptPromiseResolver`, `ScriptPromise::FromV8Value`) walks each resolution value's prototype chain without running script, and flags a `then` accessor, a Proxy, or a legacy platform object (Blink objects with named or indexed interceptors). It also counts ordinary thenables. A build flag applying the proposal's deferral was checked on a local test page. I loaded a seeded random sample of 6,000 root pages from the October 2026 crawl (300 per rank bucket and client) in that build; 5,512 loaded. Separately, a search of HTTP Archive's ~20k-page sample found 11 pages whose scripts define a `then` getter, and I loaded those too.
>
> | | Pages |
> |---|---|
> | Loaded | 5,512 |
> | Resolved a Web IDL promise with a value whose `then` lookup could run script | 0 (95% upper bound 0.054%, unweighted) |
> | Resolved with an ordinary thenable (`then` still called in the same microtask) | 656 |
>
> The `then` getters found in page scripts (SvelteKit's lazily thenable objects, a video player library) didn't reach Web IDL promise resolution on any of the 11 pages. Pages were loaded without interaction, so resolutions that only happen after user input aren't covered, and there is no use counter for a field rate.
>
> Details: [README](https://github.com/noamr/webidl-safe-resolve-compat-1645/blob/main/README.md)
